objectives.title: Root on the node
objectives.prompt: From the player's namespace-bound access (create workloads and exec into them in badpods), get root on the node and read /root/flag.txt.
hints: The cluster has no Pod Security admission: nothing stops a pod from asking for host access.
Bad Pods' README lists eight pod specs, from everything-allowed to nothing-allowed. Which host settings would you ask for first?

steps.title: Know your foothold
steps.prompt: Which Kubernetes resource may the player create in the badpods namespace, the one Bad Pods is built around? (singular)

steps.title: Pick a host namespace
steps.prompt: Which pod spec field shares the node's process namespace with the pod?

objectives.title: Everything allowed
objectives.prompt: The everything-allowed Bad Pod mounts the node's root filesystem. At which path inside the container?
hints: Read the volumeMounts of the everything-allowed pod manifest.

objectives.title: Privileged and hostPID
objectives.prompt: With privileged and hostPID, which utility enters the namespaces of the node's PID 1 to give a shell on the node?
hints: It is a util-linux tool that enters other processes' namespaces.

objectives.title: Privileged only
objectives.prompt: A privileged pod without hostPath still sees the node's devices. In which directory of the container do the node's disks appear?
hints: A privileged container gets every device of the node: where do Linux devices live?

objectives.title: hostPath only
objectives.prompt: With a hostPath mount of the node's filesystem, which file on this k3s node holds the cluster-admin kubeconfig?
hints: k3s writes its admin kubeconfig under /etc/rancher.

objectives.title: hostPID only
objectives.prompt: With hostPID you can see every process on the node. Which file under /proc/<pid>/ exposes a process's environment variables?
hints: Secrets are often passed to processes as environment variables.

objectives.title: hostNetwork only
objectives.prompt: A hostNetwork pod sits on the node's network, not the pod network. Which Kubernetes traffic control does that let it sidestep?
hints: Think of the resource that restricts which pods may talk to which.

objectives.title: hostIPC only
objectives.prompt: With hostIPC, which shared-memory directory of the node do you inspect for data other processes left behind?
hints: POSIX shared memory is a tmpfs under /dev.

objectives.title: Nothing allowed
objectives.prompt: Without any host access, which credential mounted into every pod by default do you check for excess permissions?
